info.title: Alpaka
info.author: MineNiteMii
info.description: A LLM loader for Nintendo Switch
info.details:
Alpaka runs local GGUF language models directly on your Nintendo Switch, using llama.cpp for inference and a custom controller-driven UI (no SDL2).

Features:
- Model picker for .gguf files on your SD card
- Streaming chat: word-wrapped bubbles, D-Pad/stick scrolling, on-screen keyboard input
- Multiple saved chats per model, resumable anytime
- Inline markdown: bold, inline code, fenced code blocks
- CPU-only llama.cpp inference with a lighter, repetition-resistant sampler

CPU-only for now - expect ~1-3 tok/s depending on model size, a Tegra X1 memory-bandwidth limit, not a UI bottleneck (steady 59-60 FPS during generation). GPU acceleration is in progress.

Open source, built on llama.cpp/ggml and libnx. See the GitHub repo for build instructions and source.

changelog:
v0.5.0 - Initial GUI release, replacing the console prototype's printf interface.

Added:
- Custom software renderer (libnx framebuffer + stb_truetype), after SDL2 proved unreliable for input on this hardware
- Model picker scanning sdmc:/switch/llm/models/*.gguf
- Streaming chat: word-wrapped bubbles, D-Pad/stick scrolling, on-screen keyboard input
- Multiple saved chats per model, stored on the SD card
- Inline markdown: **bold**, `code`, and fenced code blocks
- Real llama.cpp inference (CPU-only), ported from the console prototype
- Lighter sampler (repetition penalty + low temperature) instead of pure greedy, to reduce repetition loops
- compat.c: posix_memalign/sysconf shims for newlib

Known limitations:
- CPU-only - GPU backend (ggml-deko3d) not yet wired in
- ~1-3 tok/s depending on model size/clocks (hardware bandwidth limit, not a GUI bottleneck - 59-60 FPS held during generation)
- No markdown headers/lists/rules/italics
